we aim to identify the source term within a structural acoustic partial differential equation model, consisting of a two or three-dimensional interior acoustic wave equation with a compactly supported source term within a bounded domain. We derive a uniqueness and stability estimate for the source term based on a single measurement of the structural displacement on the boundary, establishing that the L2 norm of the source term can be estimated with a constant multiple of the sum of two reconstruction error terms, each related to a variational formulation and a data assimilation approach. A theoretical example is provided to illustrate the required regularity of the initial conditions, and a stability estimate is obtained for the linear operator linking the boundary measurement to the source term. This work is an extension of previous studies to a structural acoustic partial differential equation model and incorporates a source term that is compactly supported within a bounded domain.

By investigating the notion of Extended Double Covers of signed graphs, researchers have made a new discovery. Specifically, a signed graph is considered planar-complete if any planar signed graph that meets certain conditions has a homomorphism to it. The main conjecture is that if a signed graph is connected, has no positive odd closed walks, and is planar-complete, then its Extended Double Cover will also be planar-complete. This conjecture has significant implications and extensions, and it has already led to significant advancements in various areas of research. On the other hand, end-to-end methods that use a single system are challenging to implement due to limited data availability. We investigate zero-shot translation, a technique that enables translating unseen language pairs without requiring additional speech-to-text training data. While successful in multilingual machine translation, zero-shot translation has not been explored in the context of speech translation. Our goal is to develop zero-shot speech translation models that can learn to translate speech to text without direct training data, by leveraging existing speech and text data in other language pairs. However, the distinct representations of speech and text pose a significant challenge, particularly when it comes to learning to translate speech. Our proposed solution involves pre-training the model using contrastive learning to enhance its ability to learn the underlying audio-visual connections. We further refine the model's language capabilities through an auxiliary text-to-speech synthesis task, which enables it to learn the distributions of text and audio in a more holistic manner. These pre-training techniques are combined using a self-supervised loss function that minimizes the need for labeled data. Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves promising results in zero-shot speech translation, with improvements of up to +11.8 and +3.9 points in BLEU scores compared to direct end-to-end speech translation models and existing zero-shot speech translation baselines, respectively.

By integrating a minimal dark sector into the "missing partner" type-I seesaw framework, we derive a comprehensive model for neutrino oscillations and dark matter phenomena. This interaction enables dark matter to undergo resonant conversion into standard model neutrinos, explaining their non-absolute tiny masses. By satisfying model constraints, we determine the parameter ranges that facilitate dark matter stability, neutrino oscillation patterns, and consistency with experimental results, including direct detection, neutrinoless double beta decay, and cosmological data.

For intricate domains, direct potential calculation becomes computationally expensive due to the use of unstructured meshes. In this research, we propose an efficient and high-order method for computing Newtonian potentials by applying Green's third identity, transforming the volume integral into boundary integrals that can be easily processed by the Helsing-Ojala method or its parallelized version. This transformation significantly reduces the time required for near-field and self-interaction computations over unstructured meshes, making them comparable to the time needed for far-field interaction computation using the FMM-based method. A key component of our algorithm is the high-order approximation of a function over a mesh element, which is often considered an ill-conditioned problem due to the solution of a Vandermonde linear system. However, we demonstrate that when the function is sufficiently smooth and a backward stable linear solver is used, the resulting monomial expansion can approximate the function uniformly with a rate of O(h^p), where h denotes the mesh size and p is the degree of the expansion. We provide numerical experiments to illustrate the performance of our algorithm.
